# Competitive Report Structure

Curated by Skill Harbor: the final step of the competitive analysis pipeline. Takes scored competitor profile cards (from benchmark-methodology) and assembles them into a report that answers three questions: who do we compete with, how do we compete, and where is our defensible white-space. Opens by establishing the client's positioning brief (strategic tension, brand balance, differentiator, target quadrant), then builds an executive summary written so a founder reads only it and knows what to do, a market landscape with a multi-axis 2x2 map placing every competitor and the client, competitor tiers, a benchmarking matrix, a white-space analysis that tests whether the target quadrant is genuinely open, strategic recommendations checked against the brand balance, and team alignment trigger questions. Every section must earn its place by moving toward a decision; anything that does not gets cut. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: garbage in, garbage out; the report is only as good as the scored profile cards it assembles. Works best paired with benchmark-methodology from the same repository. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
